body:
### Description

Hi there, I've found unexpected behaviour when fitting a polynomial using an int64 array. 

It seems that a polynomial created with `p = cp.poly1d(cp.polyfit(x, y, N))` requires a float array `x` when calling via `p(x)`  -- see code example below. The output of `cp.polyfit` looks the same so `poly1d` seems to be the culprit.

(I also note that Numpy has introduced a new `polynomial.Polynomial` for fitting, so this issue may not be high priority). Thanks!

### To Reproduce

```py
import pylab as plt
import cupy as cp

# create x values using arange, default dtype is int64
x = cp.arange(1048576) - 1048576//2

# Create example polynomial to fit
x_ = x.astype('float64')
y = x_ + 0.5 * x_**2 - 0.05 * x_**3 + 0.001 * x_**4 - 0.00001 * x_**5

# Fit the polynomial
p = cp.poly1d(cp.polyfit(x, y, 5))

# Plot polynomials
plt.plot(cp.asnumpy(y))
plt.plot(cp.asnumpy(p(x_)))
plt.plot(cp.asnumpy(p(x)))

print(p(x).dtype) # prints float64 (not int64!)
print(p(x_).dtype) # also prints float64

assert np.allclose(p(x_), p(x)) # will raise an error

```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/713251/163835045-d12b136d-6318-48ad-8f20-35bcc11de6c8.png)


### Installation

Conda-Forge (`conda install ...`)
